steps.say: Digestion breaks food into pieces small enough to pass into the blood. It starts in the mouth.
Teeth chew the food: incisors cut, canines tear and molars grind. Saliva wets the food and starts to digest starch.

figure.alt: Teeth and a tongue in the mouth, where digestion begins.

steps.say: The oesophagus squeezes food down to the stomach. The stomach churns food with acid and digestive juices.

figure.alt: Food moves from the mouth down to the stomach.

steps.say: In the small intestine, food is digested further. Digested food passes through its walls into the blood.
The large intestine takes water back into the body. Waste is stored in the rectum until it leaves the body.
Fibre from plant foods helps the muscles of the gut push food along.

check.prompt: In which organ is most water taken back into the body?

options.why: The stomach churns food with acid. It takes back little water.
The oesophagus only moves food down to the stomach.
The mouth chews food and adds saliva.

hints: This happens near the end of the digestive system.
By this point, digested food has already passed into the blood.
Think about the part of the gut just before the rectum.
check.explanation: The large intestine takes water back into the body. What is left becomes solid waste.

check.prompt: The tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach is the ___.
hints: Its muscles squeeze food downwards when you swallow.
It runs down your neck and chest, behind the windpipe.
Its scientific name starts with the letters oe.
check.explanation: The oesophagus is the muscular tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
